overview: Schneider Electric is a French multinational that electrifies, automates, and digitalizes industry, buildings, infrastructure, and homes through a portfolio spanning electrical distribution equipment, industrial automation and control systems, and software (led by AVEVA). Organized into two reporting segments -- Energy Management (~83% of FY2025 revenue) and Industrial Automation (~17%) -- the Group reported record FY2025 revenue of EUR 40.2 billion, with North America, Europe, Asia Pacific and the Rest of World each contributing meaningfully. Data Center & Networks has become the single most important demand driver, as AI infrastructure build-out requires the power distribution, backup power (APC/UPS), and liquid cooling (Motivair) equipment at the core of Schneider's offer.

business_model.summary: Schneider sells a mix of Products (electrical distribution equipment, switchgear, circuit breakers -- 47% of revenue by business model), Systems (engineered power/automation systems, project-based -- c.34-35%), and Software & Digital Services (c.18-20%, increasingly subscription-based via AVEVA, EM Software, Field Services and Digital Services, collectively branded the 'Digital Flywheel,' which was 62% of H1 2026 Group revenue). Products are largely transactional/distribution-driven with high volume; Systems are project-based with longer cycles and large order backlogs; Software & Services provide the highest-margin, increasingly recurring revenue (AVEVA ARR +10-12% per year and 82% recurring as of H1 2026). The business model is split roughly 83%/17% between the Energy Management segment (electrical distribution, industrial power, secure power/data center, home & distribution) and Industrial Automation (process/discrete automation, industrial software including AVEVA, ETAP, RIB).

revenue_streams.name: Energy Management
revenue_streams.trend: growing (+10.3% organic FY2025), accelerating further in 2026 on Data Center demand

revenue_streams.name: Industrial Automation
revenue_streams.trend: recovering (+3% organic FY2025, accelerating to +8-11% organic in H1/Q2 2026 as Discrete automation and AVEVA improve)

revenue_streams.name: Systems (by business model)
revenue_streams.trend: fastest-growing, led by Data Center-related Systems orders

revenue_streams.name: Software & Digital Services incl. AVEVA
revenue_streams.trend: growing, ARR +10-12%, transitioning to subscription (SaaS outgrowing on-premise)

business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2B: industrial and commercial enterprises, data center/hyperscale operators and colocation providers, utilities/grid operators, contractors/panel builders/distributors (1.4M+ partner network), OEMs, and some B2C exposure through residential electrical products and the new Schneider Home offer
business_model.geographic_mix: North America (Energy Mgmt EUR 13.9bn, Industrial Automation EUR 1.6bn in FY2025), Western Europe (EUR 7.4bn / EUR 1.9bn), Asia Pacific (EUR 8.3bn / EUR 2.2bn), Rest of World (EUR 3.6bn / EUR 1.3bn) -- a well-diversified four-region, four-hub model with no single country dominating

main_competitors: Rexel/Sonepar (distribution partners, also co-defendants in French cartel case)
competitive_position.market_position: #1 position in electrical distribution across all four end markets served (Data Center & Networks, Buildings, Industry, Infrastructure) per company disclosure; #1 in grid digital solutions and #1 in industrial data/safety software; most complete liquid-cooling-plus-electrification portfolio for AI data centers following the Motivair acquisition; present in 1 of every 4 buildings and used by 20 of the top colo/hyperscale cloud providers

moat_factors.description: EcoStruxure is an open, IoT-enabled architecture spanning product-to-cloud; the vast installed base of switchgear, breakers, and automation hardware creates long replacement cycles, a sticky services/software upsell channel, and high switching costs for integrated industrial customers

moat_factors.factor: Breadth of integrated portfolio (electrification + automation + software)
moat_factors.description: Few competitors can offer grid-to-chip-to-chiller solutions spanning power distribution, UPS/backup power, liquid cooling, industrial automation and software (AVEVA, ETAP, Cognite pending) under one roof, which is increasingly valuable for complex AI data center and industrial projects

164 factories, 85 distribution centers, and a multi-hub (North America/Europe/India/China) supply chain moving toward ~90% regional sourcing/manufacturing gives cost and tariff resilience versus smaller rivals

Decades-long relationships with 1.4M+ electricians/contractors/panel builders and distributors (Rexel, Sonepar) create a deep go-to-market moat, though the same distributor relationships were the subject of the French price-fixing fine

AVEVA's transition to subscription (82% of agnostic software revenue recurring as of H1 2026) is building a more durable, higher-margin revenue stream, though it remains a minority of total Group revenue

weaknesses: Industrial Automation/Discrete automation segment has been cyclically weak for several years (only now recovering) and remains far smaller and lower-growth than Energy Management, concentrating most incremental earnings growth in one segment
Heavy and growing reliance on Data Center & Networks demand (30% of FY2025 orders and the primary driver of recent beats) creates concentration risk if AI capex cools

History of anticompetitive conduct findings (EUR 207m French Competition Authority fine in the electrical distribution sector, under appeal) highlights channel-conflict and pricing-collusion risk inherent to the distributor-heavy go-to-market model
Residential/Buildings-exposed Products demand has been structurally soft in several developed markets (Germany, UK, France) for multiple years
Integration risk from a rapid string of large, recent acquisitions (Motivair, Planon, Cognite, AiDASH, and now PTC) increases execution complexity simultaneously across multiple deals

growth_drivers: AI/data center infrastructure supercycle: triple-digit demand growth in Data Center and Semiconductor end-markets in Q2 2026, Systems orders accelerating, and a liquid-cooling plus 800VDC power portfolio purpose-built for next-generation AI factories (partnerships with Nvidia, Foxconn, SoftBank's French AI infrastructure build-out, and a new Dunkirk data-center power-module plant)

Pending acquisition of PTC for ~$22.6bn (announced October 5, 2026, expected close Q3 2027) -- Schneider's largest-ever deal, adding industrial software/PLM capabilities (CAD, PLM, IoT) with ~EUR 2.4bn revenue and ~40% adjusted EBITA margin, and ~EUR 250m of targeted annual synergies by year three

Pending acquisitions of Cognite (agnostic industrial data/agentic AI platform, $3.1bn, announced June 30, 2026) and AiDASH (AI-powered vegetation/asset/climate risk intelligence for utilities, ~90% stake, announced July 30, 2026), both expanding the 'Energy & Industrial Intelligence' software stack
AVEVA's continuing subscription transition (ARR +10-12% annually) and broader 'Digital Flywheel' (62% of H1 2026 revenue) shifting revenue mix toward higher-margin, more recurring streams

Grid modernization and electrification megatrend: addressable market estimated to grow at 6-7% CAGR to over EUR 600bn by 2030, driven by renewables integration, decentralized/Prosumer energy models, and grid resilience investment
Regionalization of manufacturing (~90% target for regional sourcing/production) supporting tariff resilience and faster delivery as reshoring accelerates

Operational excellence / 'Advancing Energy Tech' company program: pricing discipline, productivity (+EUR 535m delivered H1 2026), and Support Function Cost ratio improvement (-1.2pt in H1 2026) driving margin expansion ahead of revenue growth

Capital allocation discipline: progressive dividend (16th consecutive year of increases, EUR 4.20/share for FY2025, +8% YoY) and a new systematic share buyback program (EUR 249m repurchased as of June 30, 2026) supporting shareholder returns alongside M&A

business.risk: Concentration in Data Center end-market demand
business.description: Data Center & Networks was 30% of FY2025 orders and the primary driver of the 2026 upside; a slowdown in AI capex or hyperscaler spending would disproportionately hit growth and could strand recently added liquid-cooling/power-module capacity
Discrete and Process & Hybrid automation markets have been volatile and only recently resumed growth after a multi-year downturn tied to customer capex deferrals and commodity price volatility

business.risk: Integration of a rapid sequence of large acquisitions
business.description: Motivair, Planon, Cognite, AiDASH and now PTC (the largest deal in company history at $22.6bn) are being integrated concurrently; execution missteps, culture clashes, or overpaying (PTC at a 42% premium) could destroy value or distract management

Digital giants, software players, and energy majors are entering energy-efficiency and digital services markets Schneider currently serves, while local/regional players compete for agnostic, open-architecture business

financial.description: EUR 32.7bn of FY2025 revenue (over 80%) was in foreign currencies, including EUR 15.1bn in USD and EUR 4.3bn in CNY; management estimates a 10% EUR appreciation vs. USD would reduce adjusted EBITA by ~EUR 427m; FY2026 FX is currently guided as a EUR 300-500m revenue headwind

financial.risk: Rising net debt / leverage from M&A
financial.description: Net debt rose from EUR 11.98bn (June 2025) to EUR 15.36bn (June 2026), with Net Debt/Adjusted EBITDA at 1.64x; the PTC deal (funded via a mix of equity and new debt) and other pending acquisitions will add further leverage, though A-grade credit ratings have so far been reaffirmed

12% of trade and other operating receivables were overdue as of year-end 2025 (EUR 1,229m), with EUR 425m overdue by more than three months; wide customer/geographic diversification and credit insurance mitigate this

financial.risk: Raw material and tariff cost inflation
financial.description: H1 2026 gross margin absorbed a net price headwind of EUR -154m, including a EUR -330m raw material headwind and EUR -104m net tariff impact, partly offset by EUR +280m of product pricing

regulatory.description: French Competition Authority fined Schneider Electric EUR 207m (part of a EUR 470m total fine against Schneider, Legrand, Rexel and Sonepar) in October 2024 for anticompetitive practices in electrical distribution from 2012-2018; Schneider has appealed, and a parallel criminal case remains unresolved as of the most recent disclosure

regulatory.risk: Antitrust/regulatory approval risk on pending M&A
regulatory.description: The PTC, Cognite, and AiDASH transactions are all subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals across multiple jurisdictions, creating deal-completion risk and timing uncertainty (PTC not expected to close until Q3 2027)

As a multinational operating in 100+ countries with some dual-use-capable products, Schneider is exposed to evolving export control and sanctions regimes, particularly amid US-China technological decoupling

regulatory.risk: Human rights/supply chain due diligence (CS3D, Forced Labour Regulation, Duty of Vigilance)
regulatory.description: Over 40 duty-of-vigilance-related legal cases were pending at end-2025; EU CS3D and Forced Labour Regulation compliance obligations are phasing in through 2027-2028

macro.description: US-China decoupling, tariffs, and a more multi-polar trade environment increase compliance costs and could disrupt the Group's historically globalized supply chain, despite the multi-hub regionalization strategy
Buildings end-market demand (29% of FY2025 orders) is explicitly guided to 'track macroeconomic trends,' and Residential markets have been a drag in multiple geographies
Management flagged potential H2 2026 pressure on global supply chains and inflation from Middle East disruption as a specific, named macro risk in the H1 2026 outlook
Volatile commodity prices have contributed to delayed industrial customer investment decisions, particularly in Process & Hybrid automation markets

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Addressable market for electrification, automation and digitalization estimated at EUR 600bn+ by 2030, growing 6-7% CAGR 2025-2030, driven by three mega-trends: the new energy landscape (electrification/decarbonization), digitalization & AI (data center/compute growth), and a more decentralized, multi-polar world (reshoring, grid resilience). Data Center & Networks is the standout sub-segment with market CAGR cited above 10% through 2030.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. Energy Management (Systems, Infrastructure, Data Center) has been resilient and AI-driven; Industrial Automation (Discrete, Process & Hybrid) is more exposed to industrial capex cycles and has swung from downturn to recovery over 2023-2026; Buildings/Residential tracks macro/construction cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity via industrial capex, construction/real estate demand, and the cost of financing a leveraged M&A program (net debt rose materially in H1 2026 ahead of further announced deals)
key_input_costs: Steel and raw materials for switchgear/enclosures
Labor/SFC costs, partly offset by productivity programs

recent_developments.event: Reported record Q3 2026 revenue of EUR 11.46bn, up 16.9% organic (ahead of ~EUR 11.13bn consensus), with Energy Management up ~19% organic and Industrial Automation up ~8% organic; nine-month revenue reached EUR 32.7bn, up 15% organic. Raised FY2026 guidance to organic revenue growth of +12% to +14% (from +10% to +13%) and adjusted EBITA growth of +18% to +21% (from +14% to +19%), with margin expected up 100-120bps organic. Shares slipped despite the beat, in part on valuation and digestion of the just-announced PTC deal.

Announced agreement to acquire U.S. industrial software company PTC for approximately $22.6bn ($205/share, a 42.3% premium; ~$23.7bn enterprise value) -- Schneider's largest acquisition ever. PTC serves 30,000+ customers with ~EUR 2.4bn FY2025 revenue and ~40% adjusted EBITA margin; deal expected to close by Q3 2027 and to generate ~EUR 250m of annual run-rate synergies by year three, funded via a mix of equity and new debt.

Reported H1 2026 results: revenue EUR 21.2bn (+14.0% organic), gross margin 42.5% (+10bps organic), Adjusted EBITA margin 19.3% (+120bps organic), net income (Group share) EUR 2.5bn (+30%), free cash flow EUR 1.6bn (+244%, or +140% excluding a one-off French fine payment in H1 2025). Upgraded FY2026 target to organic revenue growth of +10% to +13% and adjusted EBITA growth of +14% to +19% (subsequently raised again in October). Announced agreement to acquire AiDASH (~90% of share capital), an AI-powered critical-infrastructure/utility software company.

Announced agreement to acquire Cognite, an agnostic industrial data and agentic AI platform, for $3.1bn, to be integrated into the 'Energy & Industrial Intelligence' software stack alongside AVEVA, ETAP, and the newly acquired PTC and AiDASH assets.
Paid FY2025 dividend of EUR 4.20/share (+8% YoY), the 16th consecutive year of progressive dividend increases, following shareholder approval at the May 7, 2026 AGM.

Reported record FY2025 results: revenue EUR 40.2bn (+8.9% organic, first time crossing EUR 40bn), Adjusted EBITA margin 18.7% (+50bps organic), net income (Group share) EUR 4.2bn (-2% reported, impacted by a one-time France competition fine and associate impairment), free cash flow EUR 4.6bn (111% cash conversion), Adjusted EPS EUR 8.59 (+3%). Energy Management revenue EUR 33.1bn (83% of Group, +10.3% organic); Industrial Automation revenue EUR 7.0bn (17% of Group, +3.0% organic).

Unveiled an integrated Motivair-branded liquid cooling portfolio (CDUs, rear-door heat exchangers, dynamic cold plates, chillers) for AI/HPC data centers, following the February 2025 closing of Schneider's controlling (75%) investment in Motivair Corporation (announced October 2024, ~$850m), with expanded manufacturing capacity in Buffalo NY, Italy, and India aimed at tripling output.

Systematic share buyback program (announced at the 2025 Capital Markets Day) under execution: EUR 249m repurchased as of June 30, 2026, alongside continued A/A-1 (S&P) and A2 (Moody's) investment-grade credit ratings, both re-affirmed following the Cognite transaction announcement.

French Competition Authority fined Schneider Electric EUR 207m (part of a EUR 470m total fine with Legrand, Rexel and Sonepar) for anticompetitive pricing practices in electrical distribution (2012-2018); Schneider appealed the decision on December 19, 2024, and the appeal remains pending as of the FY2025 Universal Registration Document (filed March 2026). A related criminal case in France also remains open.

items.notes: Third upgrade of the year, following a record Q3 (revenue +16.9% organic) driven by Data Center, Semiconductor and broad-based end-market demand
Implied by combination of revenue growth and margin improvement; to be achieved via operating leverage, pricing, and productivity
As of the H1 2026 guide this implied adjusted EBITA margin of approximately 19.4%-19.7%; the October update implies further upside given the larger bps range
Driven mainly by USD and INR weakness vs. EUR; FX impact on adjusted EBITA margin estimated as roughly flat

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Olivier Blum described H2 2026 expectations as 'all 4 end markets to drive growth, with Data Center & Networks to sustain strong momentum' and 'all 4 regions to contribute to growth, led by U.S. and India,' while flagging 'disruption in the Middle East to impact H2, with potential for pressure on global supply chains and increased inflation' as a specific risk. Management reiterated an unchanged set of CEO priorities ('Technology Leadership, Customer Differentiation, Operational Excellence') under the 'Advancing Energy Tech' company program, with explicit commitments to retain category-A credit ratings, continue the progressive dividend policy, pursue active portfolio management (acquisitions in fast-growing technology and geographies), and continue the systematic share buyback program alongside the expanded M&A agenda (Cognite, AiDASH, PTC).

bull_case: Direct, multi-product exposure to the AI/data center infrastructure buildout -- power distribution, UPS/backup power, and liquid cooling (Motivair) -- with triple-digit demand growth in Data Center and Semiconductor end-markets and a purpose-built 800VDC/liquid-cooling product roadmap aligned with Nvidia-generation AI factories

Three consecutive upward guidance revisions in 2026 (organic revenue growth raised from the original target to +10-13% to +12-14%; adjusted EBITA growth raised from +14-19% to +18-21%) demonstrate genuine, broad-based momentum rather than one-off strength, with record Q3 2026 revenue beating consensus

Aggressive, well-capitalized expansion of the software/industrial-intelligence stack via PTC ($22.6bn), Cognite ($3.1bn) and AiDASH, building toward a more complete, higher-margin 'Energy & Industrial Intelligence' platform that could materially shift the long-term revenue mix toward recurring software (AVEVA ARR already growing 10-12% annually)

#1 market positions in electrical distribution across all four end markets, a 1.4M+ partner network, and a regionalized (approaching ~90% local sourcing/manufacturing) supply chain provide resilience and scale advantages that are difficult for smaller or less diversified competitors to replicate

Disciplined, multi-pronged capital allocation -- 16 consecutive years of dividend growth, an active buyback program, and A-grade credit ratings maintained even through a historically large M&A wave -- signals balance-sheet confidence and shareholder-friendly management
bear_case: Growth is increasingly concentrated in Data Center & Networks demand (30% of FY2025 orders, the single largest driver of 2026 upside); any slowdown in AI capex, hyperscaler spending, or a pause in power-constrained data center buildouts would disproportionately hit the growth narrative the stock is now priced for

An unprecedented pace of large acquisitions in a single year (Motivair, Planon, Cognite, AiDASH, and the $22.6bn PTC deal, Schneider's largest ever) creates meaningful integration, cultural, and capital-allocation execution risk, while rising net debt (Net Debt/EBITDA up to 1.64x by June 2026, before PTC even closes) could pressure the balance sheet if growth decelerates

Industrial Automation remains structurally weaker and more cyclical than Energy Management, and its recent recovery (+3% organic FY2025, improving through 2026) has not yet proven durable through a full industrial capex cycle

Regulatory/legal overhang from the EUR 207m French Competition Authority fine (under appeal) for anticompetitive distribution practices, plus a parallel unresolved criminal case, highlights channel and pricing risk embedded in the company's heavy reliance on a small number of major distributors (Rexel, Sonepar)

Substantial currency exposure (over 80% of revenue in foreign currencies, with USD and CNY the largest) and tariff/raw-material cost volatility (H1 2026 saw a EUR -330m raw material and EUR -104m net tariff headwind to gross margin) mean reported results can diverge meaningfully from underlying organic performance, complicating valuation at a premium multiple with Strong Buy consensus already priced for continued upside
